verdict.tagline: Brilliant survival horror that survives its initial technical stumbles.
for_you_if: you love classic survival horror reimagined
you want an unbroken journey through the Ishimura
not_for_you_if: you encounter controller and menu bugs
you need stable performance during room transitions
you struggle with alt-tab freezing issues

claims.claim: Reviewers encounter input issues where controllers fail to be recognized or work properly.

citations.review_text: Well this is crap. controller support doesn't work. Sprint either. keyboard remapping sucks. game looks nice but can't play it due to poor controls.

I've played for 18 minutes and all of that was spent trying to get it to recognize any input from my Xbox Elite 2 controller. Search around and apparently many people have trouble getting this game to work with a controller. I've tried wired, wireless, a different controller entirely, enabling/disabling steam input, etc.

Loaded it up and half the controls don't work and neither does my controller. I did some reading online and there's a potential fix if I mess with various settings and download third party programs. Or, I could play something that just works and not this EA garbage.

Looks way worse than the OG, the atmosphere has suffered a lot too. The videos don't really show it, but ingame, stuff looks like a Walmart cashgrab. Everything's plasticky and tidy, smoothed monsters, the looming shadows are gone, and actors feel like cheap knock-offs. HAMMOND USED TO BE PETER MENSAH FOR CRYING OUT LOUD! Not to mention that right off the bat, if you change some controls from keyboard to mouse, you get the infamous "I can turn only to the right" bug. 

Man... I don't want to see what else this has in store, 15 minutes was enough.

I waited for a heavy discount because I didn't believe a timeless legend such as the OG at hand, made with visuals that could already stand the test of time for eternity, needed any remake. I was right. It didn't. And certainly not this one.

The game has beautfiful graphic but before long you'll get into one major fight and it's not the aliens. It's the menus. They respond rather slowly but do actually register your input so when getting to the next screen it already goes somewhere else. And every menu has an animation to open, from the Esc menu to the map to the inventory management you'll fight it all.

It irked me more than I thought it would and decided to give the game a pass

Game has a game breaking bug where it unloads a bullet every time you reload or press esc on an interactable in game menu, or the main in game menu. And I'm pretty sure you this actually makes the story unplayable as you don't get that many bullets. Never was refunded. SMH

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features an integrated map and navigation system accessed via a button press to guide player movement.

citations.review_text:
Just finished Dead Space, and after playing The Callisto Protocol right before it, I can finally compare them properly.

First of all, the sprint button actually works as a sprint button. Huge plus. Sorry, Callisto Protocol, but making me hold Shift the entire time was criminal.

One thing I absolutely loved was the navigation system. Pressing X shows you exactly where you need to go. You are much less likely to get lost or accidentally miss where you are supposed to go. It is especially useful because you revisit the same areas throughout the game, so knowing where to go saves a lot of unnecessary wandering.

Pros

Excellent navigation system
Great graphics
Really good enemy variety
A lot of different weapons
Excellent combat
Great story
Fantastic music and sound design
interesting environment and level design
Challenging without feeling unfair

The secondary weapon abilities are absolutely banger. Being able to use them with Space made the combat much more fun.
 The game does a great job of making the environment feel like an actual place instead of just a collection of levels.

I also really liked the inventory system... except when I had to play ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Tetris with it.

I ended up installing a stacking mod because I was tired of having five different stacks of the same ammo taking up half my inventory. I don't consider that cheating. I just wanted to play the game instead of managing a warehouse.

 Dead Space vs. The Callisto Protocol

I think it is unfair when people use Dead Space to completely trash The Callisto Protocol. They are similar games, but Callisto still does some things extremely well, especially visually.

If I had to rank the three similar games I have played:

Overall

1. Cronos: The New Dawn
2. Dead Space Remake
3. The Callisto Protocol

Graphics

1. The Callisto Protocol
2. Cronos: The New Dawn
3. Dead Space Remake

Gameplay, story, and things you can do

1. Cronos: The New Dawn
2. Dead Space Remak…

An excellent survival horror experience with an incredible atmosphere. Lighting, sound design, environmental details, and oppressive sense of isolation make every area feel genuinely unsettling.
The combat is intense and satisfying, especially with the focus on strategic dismemberment. Every encounter feels dangerous without becoming repetitive.
The horror also comes from the environment rather than relying entirely on jump scares. Strange noises, flickering lights, dark corridors, and subtle environmental details constantly create tension.
Level design and visual storytelling are also fantastic. Different areas feel distinct, and the way the environment guides exploration while revealing details through the surroundings is really well done.
The real challenge isn't simply overcoming fear, it's resource management and making use of the environment around you. Every bullet, healing item, and piece of equipment matters. Knowing when to fight, when to conserve resources, and even using environmental objects to your advantage can make the difference between surviving an encounter and running out of options. It adds another layer of tension and strategy to the experience.

氛围感非常出色的生存恐怖游戏。灯光、音效、环境细节，还有那种压迫感十足的孤立感，让游戏里的每个区域都让人觉得很不安。
战斗也做得很好尤其是肢解机制，让每次遇到敌人时都不能太过随意。每一场战斗都有一定的危险性，但不会让人觉得过于重复。
游戏的压迫感也不纯靠惊吓。声音、忽明忽暗的灯光、昏暗的走廊，以及各种不起眼的环境细节，都在不断制造紧张感。
关卡设计和视觉叙事同样很出色。不同区域都有自己的特点，而环境在引导玩家探索的同时，也会通过周围的细节慢慢透露出一些信息，这种设计非常自然。
游戏真正困难的地方，并不只是克服恐惧，而是资源管理，以及如何利用周围的环境。每一发子弹、每一个治疗道具、每一件装备都很重要。什么时候应该战斗，什么时候应该节省资源，以及如何利用环境中的物体来取得优势，都可能决定一场战斗是能够活下来，还是最后陷入无计可施的境地。

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the PC version experiences stutters during room transitions and when entering new areas.

citations.review_text:
The Dead Space remake is graphically and gameplay-wise a really solid update to the original Dead Space. It hits all the major notes of what a remake/remaster should be: bring the game into the modern era with a fresh coat of paint and some quality-of-life improvements, but don't change too much so that you can keep what made the original special. Dead Space still delivers disgusting levels of necromorph gore and dismemberment, intense survival horror action, and an intriguing story about cults and corporate corruption.

Two major gripes (three if you count EA being bought out by Saudi Arabia, ♥♥♥♥ you EA another reason to hate you). 1) while the final boss has been updated a little bit in terms of gameplay, I feel like they could have done more to really set it apart. They did a lot to the asteroid shooting sections to make it feel new and exciting, but the final boss still felt too similar to the simplicity of the original to be exciting and climactic like it should be. 2) the PC performance is very stuttery during room transitions. I played on medium or high graphics (can't remember) with zero motion blur and dynamic resolution scale on and found that entering a new room (even one I had previously been to) regularly caused the game to stutter for about half a second, which can be detrimental if there's something waiting for you in that doorway. I also experienced three crashes total in the final two chapters (nowhere else in my playthrough).

Dead Space remake is really solid and at a discount is a worthwhile pickup compared to the original Dead Space. I would just recommend ensuring you have a mid-to-high-end PC and do some research about Saudi Arabia and the ethics of its buy-out of much of the gaming world.

When the Game released. Pirated it. 

When the game went on sale bought it immediately with the deluxe edition. 

One thing.. tho.. 

THE GAME HAS STUTTERING ISSUES ! 

IT WILL STUTTER EVERY TIME YOU GO FROM A NEW REGION OF THE MAP TO ANOTHER EVEN IF YOU GO TO NEW AREAS ! 

otherwise 9/10

Having played the original release on PS3, my memory was fuzzy about this game, but it quickly came back to me. All the same horror vibes, the great feeling running around, the sense of hoplessness. All great. It runs and looks really good too, if a little stuttery when first getting into new areas. My main issue has been a lack of ammo. Only carry a few weapons and you're guaranteed to pick up just their ammo type. And remember to use monsters own chopped off limbs against them, they can instakill.

claims.claim: Reviewers report performance stutters and lag when the game loads new areas or enters specific rooms like engineering.

citations.review_text:
Game has a few performance problems I have run into that seem to be area specific. Usually the game just stutters a bit when entering a new area that has to load, but nothing that actually impacts gameplay when roaming around. With the one exception being chapter 3 in the engineering room. For some reason this one room causes the game stutter for the entire stay. Thankfully this section of the game, and chapter is really short.

Outside of that one issue the game is incredibly fun and well worth the price if you can get it on sale.
Gameplay mechanics are fun, level design is great and the interconnected feeling of the ship makes back tracking feel like less of a chore and something you occasionally want to do to unlock the different access doors scattered throughout the ship decks. The sound design for the game was something I really noticed, and the ambient music that plays throughout the quieter moments of the game remind of "The Thing" in a really nice way. 

Going at a leisure pace the game should take you about an hour a chapter for around a complete playthrough of 12 -14 hours.

The Game is a pretty stuttery mess, playable but not so enjoyable.

I've played this on a modded 32GB Steam Deck LCD & 32GB Steam Machine.

To go into context, EA did a fantastic 'Remake' of Dead Space & putting a modern touch to the game. The story is still good as ever, as well as, the gameplay, functions & UI/interface. The game is good & nearly as true to the original but with modern touches.

My review is a bit on the mixed side, I would recommend to play it BUT I also feel that this game was abandoned by EA because it "Didn't meet their goals" & wouldn't exactly advocate to buy this hot mess of a game.

Since I use 'Steam' Hardware, naturally I'm using AMD Graphics Card Presets so this will be in my opinion of how it runs on those hardware.

First, when the game first came out it was "Deck Verified" when I bought it on first release but now has changed to "Playable" since then. I feel that this game can be played on the Steam Deck but I wouldn't recommend it. The game is EXTREMELY Stuttery/Laggy when you play on the Deck no matter what you do. Even if you use a Mod to patch it, it still doesn't really help with with it constantly stuttering while playing.
Imagine trying to kill a hoard of necromorph's with Medium/Low health where there is no save point (Or you try to do the permadeath mode)  & suddenly it  stutters like crazy to the point where it kills you.
That was my gameplay constantly on the Steam Deck.

For the Steam Machine, it runs much better than the Steam Deck but it still stutters I would say 3x out of 10 compared to the Steam Deck where it Stutters 5/6x out of 10. The game runs much better but as I stated, I feel that EA pretty much abandoned this game, so no matter how much you try to optimize the settings & use mods to correct the stutter, the game was just Horribly Optimized for PC. Maybe it runs better on Nvidia Graphics Cards but sadly I don't own a high enough model to test the game on, so I can't speak for how it runs on those.

All in all,…

Stays close enough to the original, while making reasonable changes like the zero-g mechanics are much better in the remake, weapons have been rebalanced, and making Issac talk makes all the dialogue scenes feel more natural.
Some characters have been changed for the better or given more spotlight (Kendra, Cross, Temple).
Nicole being a senior officer finally looks like someone who went through all the career stages (in the original she didn't even look thirty).
Some characters feel worse (Hammond).
The story includes now elements that would have been normally revealed in the second game. This was a good move. Make the story feel more... whole.
Movement feels much better and there is visible damage to the flesh which also informs the player how close he is to removing a limb from an enemy.
Enemy presence feels less opressive now. Fights seem easier and AI feels not as aggressive in their approach.
I had to install the game on a HDD. There was some stuttering when new areas were loaded in, but overall the experience was ok. Still, I would recommend playing it on SSD.
Overall worth playing at least once. if you haven't played Dead Space at all I would recommend the remake over the original.

Got 27 Hours out of the game.
Graphically amazing, but like others have said - the traversal stuttering is very distracting.
Makes you wonder what kind of Play Testing/QC is done. Surely the developers were aware of it.
It's not my Rig, with a 14700K, 64GB DDR5, 4080 Super, and installed on my Samsung 860.
No matter what settings I used, the stuttering remained, so I decided to stick with 4K.
The Gameplay does get a little predictable after a while, and the abundance of ammo crates tells you what is coming, plus the long corridors, and junctures.
Still recommend it, I did enjoy it, but the stuttering was distracting, and spoilt the immersion.
A very good remaster, even added some extra content and secrets to the game. A very good direction to take a classic in. A tad choppy with the FPS every now and then but still playable.
great gameplay and visuals and story, only bad thing is traversal microstutters, more noticeable at some points

Recommended, because it looks/plays great and keeps the spirit of the original game.  I am on my third play through, so I definitely got my money's worth.  Other than some minor stutters when entering a new area, I have no complaints.  It's a great remake.

Extremely late to the party at this point but the game is totally worth it. 

Sound design is excellent, Weapons in this game carry that strong ' oomph ' when fired which is a must when your game revolves around shooting. 

I love the addition of side quests. Exploration is rewarding without feeling dragged out, with some minor exceptions for achievement hunting. But even then it's tame enough. 

I've never had issues with performance, stable FPS all throughout. But I have had stutters in-game when loading between different sectors of the map. But that was understandable given how this game never had a loading screen during gameplay. With the sole exception of starting up the game. 

Game good, play it.

Now despite enjoying my time, I simply can't in good faith recommend it to others due to it's performance issues. It's a real shame because it truly is a remarkable game, but the traversal stutters really take away from the overall experience, I powered through regardless because story and atmosphere wise it's next level good. 

It's thrilling, terrifying and action packed, it's tense, gripping and makes you feel uneasy all the way through, it's exactly what you'd want from a horror experience. I exclusively played late at night in the pitch black dark alone and it was genuinely horrifying. 

In conclusion I'd say it's worth buying on a heavy sale, like it is now, for £4.99 I can look past the very evident performance issues and give it the benefit of the doubt but man If I would of paid full price for this I would of been quite upset and annoyed to say the least.  If you can get past the issues it has, then it's a fun ride, but if mirco stutters and other jank and lag pretty much ruins a game for you, I'd stay clear.

Dead Space Remake

Good:
‣ Constantly feeling vulnerable (which is good, because it’s supposed to be a horror game).
‣ Good atmosphere and suspense.
‣ Disturbing-looking enemies and gory elements.
‣ Pretty good story. Sometimes it’s predictable, sometimes not.
‣ The cast is interesting, but the main character is even more interesting, mainly because of his development throughout the game.
‣ The Ultimate Edition has some nice-looking skins.
‣ I would say it has good pacing and variety in gameplay: mainly puzzles, combat, running away from enemies, and exploration.
‣ Weapons are pretty fun to use once you understand how they work, and their upgrades are fun too.
‣ When you launch the game, it doesn’t go to the main menu but instead loads the last save.
‣ New Game Plus (NG+).
‣ No EA Launcher.

Mixed:
‣ It looks scary at first, but once you get used to the enemies and how the game tries to "scare" you, it kind of loses its horror element.
‣ It has two endings, which is great, but one is locked behind NG+. 

Bad:
‣ A lot of walking and backtracking.
‣ I needed a playthrough for some sections, not because I ran into difficulties, but because I overthought some situations.
‣ When loading a new area, the game gets laggy (it doesn’t last long, at least for me, around 5–6 seconds).

I didn't play the original or other games from the franchise, but i think the remake is a pretty solid game overall.

I can't recommend this game nearly enough to every survival horror enjoyer and anyone that seeks a game with good graphics, great story and amazing gameplay mechanics.

This remake honestly nails what made the first DS special, while genuinely improving the game rather than just slapping a new texture over the old one. The Ishimura still feels just as atmospheric, with visible improvements. The atmosphere is dense, oppressive, and packed with detail in countless places. Lighting, sound design, the general sense of dread while moving through the ship, all of it has been taken to a new level compared to the original, without losing what made the setting so iconic in the first place.

The biggest structural change: the Ishimura is now fully interconnected, and it genuinely changes how you experience the game. There's no sense of "levels" anymore, just one enormous, dead ship. You can walk from one end of the Ishimura to the other in a single unbroken route, and it makes the ship feel like an actual, lived-in (well, dead-in) location rather than a collection of disconnected levels. Backtracking to old areas with new tools and upgrades feels different when there's no artificial separation, which works in favor of both the game and immersion into it.

Combat and dismemberment got a real upgrade too with the new peeling system. Necromorphs now show layered damage as you strategically cut them apart, flesh and tendon and bone reacting differently depending on what you're shooting them with. It makes the core strategic dismemberment gameplay the series is known for feel even more visceral and satisfying than before.

The Intensity Director also deserves a mention. It keeps things from feeling scripted or predictable on repeat playthroughs, throwing in dynamic scares and environmental changes so the ship never feels fully "safe" even in areas you've already cleared.

Overall, this is a rare case of a remake that respects the original while meaningfully building on it in almost every direction: visuals, atmosphere, combat, and structure. If you're a fan of the original or just want one of the best sci-fi horror experiences available, this is …

As a Dead Space veteran and aficionado, I went into this game hoping for a faithful recreation of one of my favourite experience of all time with updated graphics and polished gameplay. I had expected that my muscle memory for this game would allow me to casually run through it while appreciating the new visuals.

Boy was I wrong. In the BEST way. 

The story, progression, and map layout are mostly the same, but with many MEANINGFUL changes big and small. The core experience remains the same as the 2008 original, but new challenges, enemy placements, story elements, and map design made it an entirely fresh experience for me. Things are similar enough that the game felt familiar, but different enough that I once again felt alone, isolated, and anxious about entering the next room. Like I was playing my favourite game for the first time again, 18 years later. I have to say this is the perfect remake. I'm incredibly thankful for the creative and design teams deciding to shake things up a bit and not just slap a new coat of paint on an already-amazing masterpiece.

The game still has some bugs, three years out of the box. I've experienced some audio glitches, one that actually locked-up the game when it transitioned into a cutscene. A couple of times I've had an enemy get stuck in a wall. The game also runs like garbage on Linux but does very well on Windows. I'm sure there are some tweaks I could have done to make the Linux experience better, but I have dualboot set-up so I don't have to.

Only thing I'm actually sad about is they didn't have Keith Szarabajka reprise his role as the VA for Terrence Kyne. That guy's voice is iconic. :(

Altogether, 10/10 experience. Convergence is at hand. We shall all be made whole.

I've never been a huge fan of survival horror, but Dead Space is my exception. Primarily, I dislike that feeling of anxiety resulting from a character being difficult to control or having little options available to deal with threats. DS strikes an amazing balance where the early game gives the player a degree of that anxiety, but it doesn't go overboard and Isaac quickly obtains powerful weapons and upgrades that make it feel more like the enemies are stuck in there with him, rather than the other way around. In this way, to me DS feels like a slightly more scary DOOM (2016) than anything, and I would absolutely recommend it to people like me who don't typically enjoy horror games.  

Additionally, I played the OG on PS3 back in the day and loved it, and this remake feels like an improvement in almost every way. Looks great. Sounds AMAZING. Highly satisfying weapons. Very well paced with lots to explore and do. The only thing I'm a little neutral on is that Isaac speaks in this one, which has pros and cons. On the plus side, you get a more expansive narrative and Isaac feels like part of the crew. On the other hand, in the OG you could sort of imprint yourself onto Isaac. When you felt like a badass, he wasn't saying anything to contradict that; whereas in the remake, Isaac will occasionally say things that remind you he's just a regular guy. Again though, I don't even view Isaac speaking as an overall negative; it's just more of an adjacent change for me.

Regardless, this is an extremely cool game that goes on sale often enough that I absolutely recommend picking it up.

- What a game! Dark, eerie, spooky, initially terrifying. Updated mechanics to fit with later games, such as Zero-G  now functioning like DS2's 360 degree movement. 
- Later on It does fall into the "survival horror trap" that many games do, that when you're decked out with plenty of ammo and healing items, it no longer becomes scary even in new, unexplored, dark areas because you know that you're going to be fine, but still, great game.

Dead Space Remake Review
Score: 10/10

The Dead Space remake is a straight-up masterpiece. It has everything you could want in a video game: incredible action, genuine horror, and unforgettable style.

While the original Dead Space was already one of my all-time favorite games, this remake completely blows it out of the water. It takes everything that made the original great and upgrades it in every way. Navigating the USG Ishimura has never felt so immersive, thanks to top-tier audio design and impressive visuals. Slaying Necromorphs with a diverse arsenal of weapons—each feeling distinct and fitting for an engineer—is immensely satisfying. The single biggest improvement for me, though, is the zero-gravity mechanics. They shifted from the clunky controls of the original to a smooth, free-roaming system that gives you complete freedom of movement.

If I had to nitpick one flaw, it’s the lack of skippable cutscenes. Having beaten the game multiple times, hearing the exact same dialogue on repeat when I just want to jump back into the gameplay can be a bit tedious. While it’s nice that you retain control of Isaac during most of these scenes, a dedicated skip option would have been a great addition.

Ultimately, the Dead Space remake is the best survival-horror shooter of all time. It achieves exactly what a remake should do—and then some. A true masterpiece.

[h1]An outstanding remake of a survival horror classic[/h1]
Recommended if you enjoy atmospheric horror, satisfying dismemberment combat, strong environmental storytelling.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]What This Game Is in 2-3 Sentences[/h2]
Dead Space is a survival horror game in which you explore the interconnected Ishimura, repair its failing systems, uncover what happened to its crew, and fight grotesque creatures by strategically cutting off their limbs. The remake retains the original story and overall level design while dramatically improving the graphics, character presentation, voice acting, zero-gravity movement, atmosphere, and optional content.

The core loop: progress through the ship, repair its systems, manage resources, complete naturally integrated side missions, and dismember enemies using repurposed engineering equipment.

What makes it interesting/unique: the targeted dismemberment system, fully diegetic interface, oppressive atmosphere, and the convincing feeling that you are an engineer trying to keep a dying ship operational.
